name: Yosemite Falls
type: Three-section fall: upper fall, middle cascades, and lower fall
detail: The National Park Service lists the total as 2,425 feet (740 m): Upper Yosemite Fall 1,430 feet, the middle cascades 675 feet, and Lower Yosemite Fall 320 feet. The park says it flows about November through July and peaks in May.

name: Sentinel Fall
detail: The park's waterfall guide lists Sentinel Falls at about 2,000 feet and says it usually flows from about March through June. The same park's natural-resource statistics page lists Sentinel Fall at 2,000 feet.

name: Ribbon Fall
detail: The National Park Service statistics page lists Ribbon Fall at 1,612 feet. The park's waterfall guide says Ribbon Fall usually runs only in spring.

name: Silver Strand Falls
detail: Listed at 1,170 feet on the park's natural-resource statistics page.

name: Horsetail Fall
detail: Listed at 1,000 feet on the park's natural-resource statistics page. This is the Yosemite Valley fall, not the other Horsetail Falls elsewhere in California.

name: Spray Falls
detail: The park says Spray Creek drops 354 feet over a lava cliff in a veil-like waterfall, fed by what remains of the Flett Glacier. Our gazetteer has a second Spray Falls in Okanogan County; this height belongs to the Pierce County fall.

name: Palouse Falls
detail: The National Park Service place page says the Palouse River drops 200 feet into a churning bowl, then runs a basalt gorge to the Snake River. The page notes the Washington Legislature named it the state waterfall in 2014. It is a state park, not a national park.

name: Ranger Falls
detail: The park describes a three-segmented waterfall with a total height of 172 feet. The tallest single drop is 73 feet.

name: Narada Falls
detail: The park says the Paradise River plunges 168 feet over an andesite lava flow.

name: Martha Falls
detail: Unicorn Creek flows from Snow Lake over a lava flow in a series of cascades, then drops 125 feet at Martha Falls.

name: Multnomah Falls
place: Columbia River Gorge National Scenic Area
detail: A National Park Service article states the falls at 620 feet and places it in the Columbia River Gorge National Scenic Area. The Forest Service recreation page for the falls did not restate a height in the copy retrieved for this update, so the 542-foot and 69-foot split quoted in older guides is not repeated here.

name: Salt Creek Falls
sourceTitle: USFS: Salt Creek Falls Observation Site
detail: The Forest Service calls it Oregon's second-highest single-drop waterfall, cascading 286 feet. There is a second Salt Creek Falls name in Alabama; this figure is the Lane County, Oregon fall.

name: ʻAkaka Falls
sourceTitle: Hawaiʻi DLNR: ʻAkaka Falls State Park
detail: Hawaiʻi State Parks says the free-falling fall plunges 442 feet into a stream-eroded gorge. The same page describes Kahuna Falls as cascading but does not give Kahuna a height.

name: Amicalola Falls
detail: Georgia State Parks says that at 729 feet, Amicalola Falls is the tallest cascading waterfall in the Southeast. A state-parks history PDF also calls it the highest cascading waterfall east of the Mississippi. That claim is about a cascade, not a single plunge.

name: Fall Creek Falls
sourceTitle: Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation: Fall Creek Falls natural area
detail: The state natural-area page says the fall plunges 256 feet. The page also calls it the highest waterfall east of the Rockies. Other agencies publish larger cascade totals east of the Rockies, including Crabtree Falls and Amicalola Falls, so that superlative depends on counting a single plunge rather than a tiered drop.

name: Whitewater Falls
detail: The Forest Service says Upper Whitewater Falls in North Carolina is a 411-foot plunge and calls it the highest waterfall east of the Rockies. The same page says South Carolina's Lower Whitewater Falls drops another 400 feet. Those are separate drops, not one measurement.

name: Lower Whitewater Falls
place: On the Whitewater River below the North Carolina falls
detail: The Forest Service page for Whitewater Falls says South Carolina's Lower Whitewater Falls falls another 400 feet. Our gazetteer does not have a separate Lower Whitewater record, so this entry links to the South Carolina state page rather than a waterfall URL.

name: Thunderhead Falls
detail: The USGS gazetteer says the falls sit 600 feet inside Thunderhead Falls tunnel and drop over a 32-foot precipice. The sentence did not match the site's usual height phrase, so it is quoted here directly.

name: Crabtree Falls
place: George Washington and Jefferson National Forests
sourceTitle: USFS: Crabtree Falls Day Use Area
detail: The Forest Service says five major cascades fall a total distance of 1,200 feet. This is the Nelson County fall on State Route 56, not the Crabtree Falls in North Carolina.

name: Taughannock Falls
sourceTitle: New York State Parks: Taughannock Falls State Park
detail: New York State Parks says the fall plunges 215 feet past cliffs that tower nearly 400 feet above the gorge.

name: Big Manitou Falls
detail: The Wisconsin DNR says Big Manitou Falls is 165 feet high. The same page calls it the fourth-highest waterfall east of the Rocky Mountains. That ranking uses the DNR's own comparison, and other agencies measure cascades differently.

name: Little Manitou Falls
detail: The DNR lists Little Manitou Falls, upstream of Big Manitou on the Black River, at 31 feet. The park's hiking page uses the name Twin Little Manitou Falls for the same 31-foot drop.

name: High Falls
sourceTitle: NPS: Visit Grand Portage State Park
detail: The National Park Service says Grand Portage State Park, managed by the Minnesota DNR and not part of the National Park System, has the highest waterfall in Minnesota, and a caption on that page reads "View of the 120 foot High Falls." The same page describes Middle Falls as a 20-foot waterfall. Our gazetteer lists Pigeon Falls in Cook County but does not give it a height, and this guide does not treat that record as the same feature.

name: Middle Falls
sourceTitle: NPS: Visit Grand Portage State Park
detail: Described on the same National Park Service page as a 20-foot waterfall on a longer trail along the Pigeon River.

name: Houghton-Douglass Falls
place: Houghton-Douglass Falls Veterans Memorial Scenic Site
detail: Michigan's recreation site page calls this Michigan's tallest waterfall and says it drops 110 feet. The page also says the path beyond the pedestrian bridge is still an undeveloped footpath without barriers.

name: Sable Falls
detail: The lakeshore says Sable Falls tumbles 75 feet over a cascading slope of Munising and Jacobsville sandstone.

name: Spray Falls
detail: The lakeshore says Spray Falls plunges about 70 feet over the cliffs directly into Lake Superior.

name: Munising Falls
detail: The lakeshore describes a 50-foot waterfall dropping over a sandstone cliff, reached by a paved 800-foot trail. In April 2025 the park posted that the Munising Falls Trail was temporarily closed after storm damage.

name: Miners Falls
detail: The lakeshore says the Miners River drops about 50 feet over a sandstone outcrop. The walk from the parking area is 0.6 miles one way.

name: Hemmed-in Hollow Falls
detail: The National Park Service says the falls cascade nearly 210 feet and calls them the highest waterfall between the Rockies and the Appalachians. The fall runs after considerable rain. The name is not in the USGS falls file this site uses, so there is no gazetteer anchor to link.

name: Smith Falls
detail: The National Park Service says Smith Falls is the tallest waterfall in Nebraska at 63 feet. The USGS gazetteer states the same 63-foot drop. The park is on the Niobrara National Scenic River and is managed by Nebraska Game and Parks.

name: Lower Falls of the Yellowstone River
sourceTitle: NPS: Canyon and the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone
detail: The park lists the Lower Falls at 308 feet (94 m). The same page says the volume over the falls can vary from 63,500 gallons per second at spring peak runoff to 5,000 gallons per second in autumn.

name: Upper Falls of the Yellowstone River
sourceTitle: NPS: Canyon and the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone
detail: The park lists the Upper Falls at 109 feet (33 m), upstream of the Lower Falls.
